answer: A water right starts on the register. The applicant files one licence point: the inlet, the staff gauge, the ditch down the knoll. A watermaster walks the headgate weekly and signs the plate; the node matches forty returns a year against the priority date, so a point that stops reading loses the seat. One point, one seat. A ferrous gate pits shut and is swapped for a serial the commissioner files, so a lifted permit copy points at a gate nobody opened. Fifty clones need fifty gated points: 1,800 filing, 6,400 ditch and pump, 900 a year compliance, 145,000 dollars before water arrives.
